title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous pages build a general 'profinite envelope' Ĉ0 of a category C0, given purely category-theoretic hypotheses (*). Ĉ0 has the same objects as C0. Its Hom(X,Y) is the completion of Hom_{C0}(X,Y) with respect to the actions of Aut(X) and Aut(Y), made into a homogeneous space under the profinite completions Aut^(X)×Aut^(Y). This is formula (17); the same construction is apparently what this page calls (12). Composition is extended by continuity, and it is unique. The target is an 'essentially profinite' category: Hom sets are locally compact, Aut groups are profinite, and Aut×Aut orbits are open.

This page applies the construction to the isotopic category of oriented anabelian surfaces of finite type. These are surfaces with negative Euler characteristic; the words 'anabéliennes' replace a crossed-out 'de t.f.'. The morphisms are presumably isotopy classes of embeddings or open immersions, as in the rest of cote 142. The result is a 'compactified profinite' category.

Grothendieck describes the Hom^ spaces topologically:
- they are topological sums of compact totally disconnected spaces, namely the closures of the countably many discrete orbits;
- hence they are locally compact, countable at infinity, totally disconnected and metrizable;
- he adds that they have no isolated points.

He then restricts to surfaces carrying a complex algebraic curve structure, i.e. X^an for X a smooth quasi-projective curve over C. On that subcategory, the Hom^_isot and their composition were defined transcendentally, through the functor X ↦ X(C). He asserts that they admit a purely algebro-geometric description, independent of the topology of C. Implicitly this goes through étale fundamental groupoids, the profinite mapping class groups as π1^ét of moduli stacks, and degenerations or boundary data for the embeddings. The last line is illegible; it probably says that for subfields of C (e.g. Q̄) there is no ambiguity.

The point of all this is to make Gal(Q̄/Q), or more generally Aut(C), act on the profinite isotopic category of surfaces. That is the 'Galois action on the Teichmüller tower' programme. The next page proves the factorisation f^ = u∘f^_0 (an iso of Ĉ0 followed by a C0-morphism) needed to define composition.
errors: 'Pas un point isolé' fails in degenerate cases. For X of type (0,3) the orientation-preserving mapping class group is finite (S3, or trivial with labelled punctures), and self-embeddings of a pair of pants are isotopic to isomorphisms. So Hom^(X,X) = Aut^(X) is finite and discrete, i.e. it consists of isolated points. More generally, any orbit whose stabiliser has finite index in a finite group gives isolated points. The claim needs a hypothesis such as an infinite mapping class group, or applies only generically.
Hom sets may also be empty; this is a trivial caveat.

The algebraic description is only asserted, not justified. Isomorphisms are fine, since π1^ét of the moduli stacks gives the full profinite completion of Mod. For non-invertible morphisms (embeddings of subsurfaces), an algebraic description needs extra input: e.g. stable curves, tangential base points, or the injectivity condition Aut_Y(Y') → Aut(Y')^ treated on the next page. None of this is proved here.

ideas.what: Profinite envelope of the isotopic category of anabelian surfaces, with Hom^ spaces being disjoint sums of profinite homogeneous spaces under Aut^(X)×Aut^(Y).
ideas.modern_name: Profinite completion of the Teichmüller tower / profinite Teichmüller groupoid (with embeddings as morphisms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); later Lochak–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Boggi
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower and its profinite completion), in outline only; not the general categorical construction

ideas.what: Topological properties of the Hom^ spaces: locally compact, σ-compact, totally disconnected, metrizable, without isolated points.
ideas.modern_name: Topology of profinite homogeneous spaces / completed Hom sets

ideas.what: For curves over C, the transcendentally defined profinite isotopy Homs and their compositions are algebraic, hence carry an action of Aut(C) and in particular of Gal(Q̄/Q).
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the profinite Teichmüller tower / étale fundamental groupoids of moduli stacks
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984); Drinfeld and Ihara for the GT group; Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme; Letter to Faltings (1983)

missed.claim: The page sketches a general functorial 'essentially profinite completion' of categories. Hom sets are completed relative to automorphism groups and composition is extended by continuity. It is applied to the isotopic category of surfaces with embeddings, not just to mapping class groupoids. The literature mostly treats profinite completions of groupoids or towers of groups, not this relative completion of a category with non-invertible morphisms.
missed.quote: il lui est donc associé une catégorie "compactifiée profinie", avec des Hom^ donnés par (12)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A minor but clean framework for treating subsurface-embedding morphisms in the profinite Teichmüller tower. It is relevant to Boggi-style congruence questions, since the injectivity condition on the next page is a separability property.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the core idea of the Esquisse programme (Galois action on the profinite Teichmüller tower), already public in outline. The topological remarks are routine, and the categorical completion is only mildly novel.
transcription_corrections: The reference after 'donnés par' is written '(12)', but given the previous page it most likely refers to formula (17).
'(par l'intermédiaire[?] d'associer ...)' probably reads '(par le biais du foncteur associant aux schémas en courbes lisses quasi-projectives sur C des surfaces topologiques orientées de t.f.)'.
The last line is uncertain; it probably reads something like 'Pour les [sous-corps] de C, pas d'ambiguïté'.
